findings.title: Live watch shows stale/global dashboard metrics when no run is active

relatedIndependentReviewFindings.note: The browser observed global or stale metrics outside an active run; the code review found that events from other run scopes corrupt the live dashboard.
The code review identified a stale live inventory overlay that can continue to override authoritative recovery after refresh.
The missing recovery aggregate helps explain why current-run outcome panels and retained telemetry can disagree after reload.

findings.description:
After a small public custom run completed, reloading `/watch` showed `No run in progress` and zero current-run reservation/outcome counts, but other live panels still displayed concrete historical values such as inventory drain, ERP confirmation timings, and consistency-lag numbers over 100 confirmed.

This makes the live dashboard internally contradictory after completion or reload: panels presented as current-run telemetry appear to carry stale or global data when there is no active run. Opus's self-audit had already identified stale Live Watch state being retained and shown as current in `opus-4.8:F8`, so this is classified as a reproduced post-fix dashboard-state issue.

findings.title: Run outcomes panel mixes terminal outcomes with live transition/pressure counters
findings.description:
During an active public custom run on `/watch`, the `Run outcomes` panel displayed terminal business outcomes such as `Confirmed` and `Failed` beside cumulative transition or pressure counters such as `Processing`, `Retrying`, and `Delayed`. The counts appeared intentional, but the panel title and description made them read as one comparable final outcome set.

Users can misread valid worker/backpressure signals as contradictory terminal outcomes while watching a surge. Opus's self-audit covered several worker and dashboard defects, but it did not identify this UI vocabulary and grouping problem.

findings.title: Watch page exposes an empty/internal load-run controls section
findings.description:
The `/watch` page rendered a visible `Load-run controls` section with a `TASK 6.4` badge and explanatory copy, but no actual controls appeared in that section. If run controls intentionally live on `/` and `/admin`, this section should not expose an empty placeholder or internal roadmap label.

The defect has low functional impact, but it makes the operator-facing page look unfinished and can confuse users searching for the promised controls. Opus's self-audit did not identify this public Watch page placeholder issue.
